procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up after cardiology. Echo per their letter: LVEF 35% (was 45% in 2015), moderate functional MR. Diagnosis now HFrEF. Since the dialysis unit dropped his target weight he sleeps on one pillow again, no night coughing, and the evening ankle swelling is much less. Still gets winded faster than a few years ago on the hill behind the barn. Weighs himself at every session.

O: Vitals per flowsheet; weight down about 2 kg since September. Fistula thrill and bruit. JVP not elevated. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema today.

A/P:
- HFrEF from anthracycline cardiomyopathy: better with volume control at dialysis. Continue lisinopril 10, furosemide 40, aspirin 81. Cardiology in a year. Told him and his wife to call for a weight jump between sessions, more pillows or swelling.
- ESRD on HD; BMP and CBC today for our records.
- Carpal tunnel R: splint, stable.
- AWV in the spring.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV (last one 2022).

Interval: no ED or hospital. HFrEF diagnosed after his fall echo; stable since target weight lowered. Discharged from sarcoma surveillance last May after 10 clean years.

HRA: independent in everything; still running the herd with help from a neighbor's son on dialysis days. No falls. PHQ-2 1 (a few days of feeling down about slowing up). Sleep okay, one pillow. Wife and he updated their health care proxies last year; ours on file is current. Never smoker, alcohol holidays only.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. Fistula thrill and bruit. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Right thigh scar without mass. No edema.

Plan:
- Labs for our records today.
- Prevention: colonoscopy due 2027. Flu and COVID each fall. Shingrix, PCV20, Tdap (2019), hep B series done. Will discuss RSV vaccine in the fall.
- HFrEF, ESRD, anemia, phos, carpal tunnel: as per recent notes, no changes.
RTC 5 to 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Adam, labs from the wellness visit look like your usual dialysis numbers. Blood count is holding steady. Nothing to change. Copy sent to nephrology.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Need refills on the lisinopril and the water pill please, same pharmacy. Thanks, Adam

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Lisinopril 10 mg and furosemide 40 mg sent to your pharmacy for 90 days with refills. Your next visit is due in September, please call to schedule.

documents.title: No-show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient did not arrive for 9:00 follow-up. Left voicemail at home number. Wife called back at 2 pm: he's finishing the last hay cut and forgot; will call to reschedule after harvest.

conditions.label: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
conditions.note: Acute decompensation; admitted for urgent hemodialysis with ultrafiltration

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, date of service 10/25/25 (Saturday). Received by fax.

CC: shortness of breath and leg swelling.

HPI: 58-year-old man with ESRD on hemodialysis three times weekly through a left forearm AV fistula and chemotherapy-related cardiomyopathy. About two months of gradually worsening breathlessness with exertion and swelling of both legs. His wife reports he has been more tired and some nights wakes short of breath. Denies chest pain, cough or fever. No recent infections. No missed sessions or changes in his dialysis schedule.

Vitals on arrival: BP 138/72, HR 102, RR 20.

Exam: JVP visible at 45 degrees. Soft systolic murmur over the precordium. Bibasilar crackles. Bilateral pitting edema to the knees. Palpable thrill over the left forearm fistula.

Impression: acute decompensated heart failure in a hemodialysis patient.

Disposition: admitted to medicine; nephrology consulted for urgent hemodialysis with ultrafiltration.

Allergies: NKDA. Home medications: calcium acetate, sevelamer, epoetin alfa, lisinopril, furosemide, aspirin 81, multivitamin, acetaminophen as needed.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called. Adam was admitted Saturday from the ED for fluid on the lungs and came home yesterday afternoon (10/28). She doesn't have discharge papers beyond a medication sheet that shows no changes. He's back on his regular dialysis schedule starting today. Breathing "way better." Denies chest pain per her. Booked post-hospital visit Tue 11/4 at 9:00. Asked her to bring whatever paperwork they have and the weight sheet from dialysis. Requested discharge summary from the hospital.

conditions.label: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here with wife. ED record from 10/25 received (ADHF; admitted for urgent dialysis with UF). No discharge summary yet despite our request. His account: three dialysis runs in the hospital, "about 5 kilos" off, discharged 10/28 with no pill changes and a lower target weight on the dialysis orders. Says it crept up on him over two months and he figured it was the harvest wearing him out (missed his September visit with us). Now breathing near his baseline, one pillow, no night waking. No chest pain. Flu and COVID shots were given at dialysis 10/8.

O: Vitals per flowsheet; weight about 5 kg below his September 2024 visit. Comfortable. JVP not elevated. Fistula thrill and bruit. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Ext: trace ankle edema.

A/P:
- Acute decompensated HFrEF, resolved after inpatient ultrafiltration. Chronic HFrEF from anthracycline cardiomyopathy, LVEF 35% (11/2024). Meds reconciled with wife's discharge sheet: no changes; lisinopril 10, furosemide 40, aspirin 81. New target weight per nephrology. Cardiology follow-up moved up to January (called their office).
- Daily weights at home on non-dialysis days, call for gain over 2 kg or more pillows.
- ESRD on HD; BMP and CBC today.
- RSV vaccine today (ESRD and HF).
- Re-request discharge summary.
RTC 3 months, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Upton on 1/20/26 after his October admission for decompensated heart failure.

He feels well, walks his property at an easy pace, sleeps flat on one pillow and denies orthopnea or nocturnal symptoms. He is meeting his new dialysis target weight.

On exam today he appears euvolemic.

Impression: HFrEF from anthracycline cardiomyopathy (LVEF 35%, 11/2024), compensated at his current target weight.
Plan: no medication changes; continue lisinopril 10 mg, furosemide 40 mg and aspirin 81 mg. Follow-up in six months.

Allergies: NKDA.
